premises.text: Unstructured-text policy communication leaves citizens without the patience to engage
premises.evidence_span: Because of this, most of us just don't have the patience to engage.

premises.text: A microsimulation engine built on merged tax and census data projects the impact of any configured policy on real people
premises.evidence_span: create a model of the US economy, where you can configure government policies and then see their projected impacts on real people

premises.text: Citizen endorsements feed government analytics and shape policy around what people want
premises.evidence_span: this response gets recorded on the government's analytics, helping them shape policies around what people want

premises.text: A turnkey solution undercuts the enormous cost of incumbent government analysis tools
premises.evidence_span: Outline, though, is a turnkey solution that not only saves governments money, but produces better governing.

domains.name: Outline simulation platform and government offer

value.text: Citizens understand and shape the government policies that affect them
value.evidence_span: making participation in government direct, intelligent, and easy

secondary_value.text: Better governing at lower cost for governments
secondary_value.evidence_span: not only saves governments money, but produces better governing

causal_links.evidence_span: it does matter. New government policy changes our income about $4,000 each year.

notes: Compact two-domain reading: the demo walk-through (personal impact, map, sliders, budget lines) is one simulation engine per v1.3.2 clarification 5, and the participation loop plus turnkey government offer are grouped with it as the single Outline offering whose parts are learned together. The $4,000 stakes figure is treated as context reinforcing the disengagement problem rather than a separate premise. Election-tool usage and procurement announcement excluded as traction.
